import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Create the scatter plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='sensor_type',
    palette='viridis', # A good colormap for distinct categories
    s=100, # Adjust point size for better visibility
    alpha=0.7, # Add some transparency to show density
    edgecolor='w', # Add white edge for better separation of points
    linewidth=0.5 # Line width for the edge
)

# Set y-axis to logarithmic scale for better price distribution visualization
# Prices often have a wide range, making a log scale more informative for relative differences.
plt.yscale('log')

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Camera Price vs. Megapixels by Sensor Type', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold')
plt.xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Price (USD, Log Scale)', fontsize=12)

# Improve legend placement
plt.legend(title='Sensor Type', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0)

# Add grid for better readability
plt.grid(True, which="both", ls="--", c='0.7')

# Adjust layout to prevent elements from overlapping
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
